name: Instabox

modes.label: Firecracker microVM (per second while running)
modes.note: Published unit rates (checked 2026-11-08): "vCPU $0.004 per vCPU-hour", "Memory $0.00225 per GiB-hour"; "Runtime is metered by the second, only while a machine is running" (instabox.sh/pricing). Billing counts "the seconds it was running (not starting, paused or stopped)" (docs/billing), so boot time is not billed. The default 4 vCPU / 8 GiB machine costs $0.034 per hour. Sizes are 2 GiB per vCPU: "Pro: 2/4, 4/8, 8/16. Builder: 2/4 up to 16/32. Team: 2/4 up to 32/64" (docs/limits); Free runs 4/8 only. The CPU basis and any overcommit are not published.

storage.note: "/data" is 20 GiB per machine (docs/limits). Free: disk at no charge, fixed at 20 GiB. Paid plans pool included disk across all machines (200 GiB Pro, 1 TiB Builder, 5 TiB Team); beyond that "allocated /data is billed at $0.08 per GiB-month ($0.00011 per GiB-hour)", billed "while it exists (running, paused or stopped)". "The system disk, snapshots and a paused sandbox's saved memory are free" (docs/billing). The pooled inclusion is modelled as 20 GiB per machine, which overstates the disk bill for fleets that stay inside the pool.

network.note: "Ingress is always free. Each plan includes egress every month (100 GiB on Free, 1 TiB on Pro, 5 TiB on Builder, 50 TiB on Team), then $0.02 per GiB" (docs/pricing). Outbound bandwidth is about 50 Mbit/s per machine (docs/limits). No per-machine public IPv4: access is through the SSH gateway and HTTPS port URLs.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: "Free gives you one 4 vCPU / 8 GiB machine to run every month at no cost" (changelog 2026-10-20); "A free sandbox is never billed, so a free month is $0.00" (docs/billing). included_usd = one 4/8 machine for 730 h at list rates (730 x $0.034), so the engine bills $0 for anything that fits. Limits (docs/limits): 1 machine in any state, 4/8 only, 20 GiB fixed disk, 5 snapshots, 200 GiB stored data, 3 starts a minute, idle pause fixed at 30 min, max run 480 min at a time followed by a cooldown (5-20 min, longer when repeated). The API also documents a monthly hours cap on the free machine "when the server enforces a cap" (credit_exhausted); its size is not published.

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: "$20/month + usage", "$20 / month free credits", "Max 100 concurrent machines", "Up to 8 vCPU / 16 GiB", "Disk up to 200 GiB", "200 GiB disk included", "Unlimited snapshots", "1 TiB egress / month" (docs/pricing). 500 machines in any state; 30 starts a minute; idle pause 5-30 min or off; max run unlimited by default (docs/limits).

plans.name: Builder
plans.note: Added 2026-11-03 (changelog). "$100/month + usage", "$100 / month free credits", "Max 200 concurrent machines", "Up to 16 vCPU / 32 GiB", "Disk up to 500 GiB", "1 TiB disk included", "5 TiB egress / month" (docs/pricing). 1,000 machines in any state; 50 starts a minute (docs/limits).

plans.name: Team
plans.note: "$500/month + usage", "$500 / month free credits", "500 concurrent machines", "Unlimited machines", "Up to 32 vCPU / 64 GiB", "Disk up to 1 TiB", "5 TiB disk included", "50 TiB egress / month", "Priority email support & SLAs" (docs/pricing). 100 starts a minute (docs/limits).

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: "Custom": "99.9% SLA", "SSO / SAML and SCIM", "Audit logs", "Dedicated pool or BYOC", "HIPAA BAA", "Dedicated support" (docs/pricing). Sizes up to 32/64 (docs/limits).

free.note: The Free plan runs one 4 vCPU / 8 GiB machine at no cost (see plans). Accounts registered before 2026-10-20 and activated before 2026-10-25 07:45 UTC keep five free sandboxes until 2026-12-01 00:00 UTC, then one (docs/pricing).

caveats: Plans since 2026-10-20 (changelog): Free $0 (one 4 vCPU / 8 GiB machine), Pro $20, Builder $100 (added 2026-11-03), Team $500, Enterprise custom. Each paid fee is usage credit of the same amount; usage beyond it is $0.004 per vCPU-hour and $0.00225 per GiB-hour, per second while running (docs/pricing).

The site shows self-service sign-up with GitHub or Google and no beta or invite wording. The API still documents an invite gate as a server switch, and paying for a plan activates a held account (OpenAPI createOrg). The 2026-10-14 launch was an invite-only beta.

Free plan limits (docs/limits): 1 machine in any state, 4/8 only, 20 GiB fixed disk, 5 snapshots, 3 starts a minute, idle pause fixed at 30 min, max run 480 min at a time with a cooldown after (5-20 min; 60-75 and 120-135 min when repeated). The API documents an unpublished monthly hours cap for the free machine "when the server enforces a cap".

Early accounts (registered before 2026-10-20, activated before 2026-10-25 07:45 UTC) keep five free sandboxes until 2026-12-01 00:00 UTC, then one runs at a time; the others are paused, not deleted (docs/pricing).

Unpublished: regions ("A machine has no `region` field in the API ... Placement is the platform's", docs/machines), SOC 2, GPU types and prices, and the CPU basis. The OpenAPI admin schema shows a scheduler CPU overcommit factor and a memory balloon; the factor is not published. Not flagged shared: there is no dedicated tier to contrast it with (Enterprise lists a "Dedicated pool or BYOC" without detail).

Marketing-only claims (homepage, not defined or measured): "You're in a new machine's shell in under a second". The docs say resume is "usually in about a second" and the android template boots "a few seconds longer than agent-browser". No measurement here; perf left to the benchmark owner.
Isolation: Firecracker microVMs on Linux 6.18.60, amd64 (docs/limits). Server source is not public.

Sizes: 2/4, 4/8, 8/16 on Pro; up to 16/32 on Builder; up to 32/64 on Team and Enterprise; 4/8 only on Free. /data is 20 GiB per machine and grows to 200 GiB / 500 GiB / 1 TiB on Pro / Builder / Team. Resizing needs a stop or a restart.

Snapshots and forks copy the disk, not memory. Fork works on a running or stopped machine (up to 5 copies per call), not a paused one. Live snapshots keep the machine running but "may leave out data programs have not written to disk yet". Pause keeps memory and processes on the same machine. No automatic periodic snapshot.

Ports: up to 16 per machine, public by default; `--private` gives a token-gated URL. A visit wakes a machine that paused itself on idle, not one you paused or stopped. Outbound bandwidth is about 50 Mbit/s per machine (docs/limits).

Secrets (2026-10-24): an outbound proxy swaps a placeholder for the real key in HTTPS headers to each Secret's allowed hosts; it does not touch URLs or bodies, and clients must trust the sandbox CA (docs/secrets).

Templates: agent-browser (default), universal, t3, herdr, orca, android (Android 14 natively, no emulator or nested VM), omarchy (Arch + Hyprland) and ci (GitHub Actions runner, `runs-on: instabox-*`). Free creates from agent-browser, android, omarchy or ci only.

Operator: the SDK is published as @insforge/instabox-sdk; instabox.sh itself does not name the company. Hosting hint only, not a public claim: api.instabox.sh resolved to an AWS EC2 address in us-west-2 (DNS, 2026-10-14).
No independent runtime/account test or performance measurement performed.

launch_post.use: Only for the fact that Instabox launched and what it claims; not evidence for any feature.
launch_post.claims: 4 vCPU, 8 GB RAM spun up in <1s; Built-in computer use; Snapshots for easy cloning; Persistent files, packages, config; Public URLs for local ports; invite-only beta; Early access includes 20 vCPU, 40GB RAM for free.
launch_post.note: Quoted from the founder's launch announcement on X (Hang Huang, @hanghuang_); the individual post URL could not be retrieved without an X login, so the profile is cited.

fleet.raise: Self-serve plan upgrade: Pro 100 running (500 total), Builder 200 (1,000), Team 500 (unlimited); Enterprise by contract.
fleet.verification: GitHub or Google sign-in. Paid plans need a card (Alipay for Pro and Builder since 2026-11-04).
fleet.tiers: Free: 1 machine, 4/8, 3 starts/min. Pro $20: 100 running, up to 8/16, 30 starts/min. Builder $100: 200 running, up to 16/32, 50 starts/min. Team $500: 500 running, up to 32/64, 100 starts/min.
fleet.notes: "Machines | Free: 1, in any state (paused and stopped ones count). Pro: 500, 100 running at once. Builder: 1,000, 200 running at once. Team: unlimited, 500 running at once" (docs/limits). exec: 32 requests at once, 10 min per command; `exec --background` has no exec timeout.

isolation.quote: on Linux 6.18.60 (`uname -r`: `6.18.60-instabox`; `6.18.60-instabox-android` on `android`, `6.18.60-instabox-drm` on `omarchy`) in a Firecracker microVM
isolation.note: Corroborated by the OpenAPI HostReport schema (node-agent field firecrackerVersion, https://api.instabox.sh/v1/openapi.json) and the homepage ("Full VM: a real virtual machine with its own kernel and root"). The server source is not public.

linux.quote: Machine A Linux VM of your own in the cloud, with its own kernel, root and Docker.

windows.quote: Every template but `ci` (Ubuntu 24.04) and `omarchy` (Arch Linux) is Debian 13 (trixie), amd64
windows.note: All eight templates are Linux; no Windows machine is documented.

macos.quote: Every template but `ci` (Ubuntu 24.04) and `omarchy` (Arch Linux) is Debian 13 (trixie), amd64

gpu.quote: `gpu` | string | none: no GPU | a GPU type your org has access to, count 1
gpu.note: Create takes a gpu field for orgs given access, but no GPU type, price or plan is published.

snapshot.quote: A paused machine keeps its memory and running programs; a stopped one keeps only its files.
snapshot.note: Pause preserves memory and processes ("If that is not possible it starts fresh: files are kept, processes are not", docs/machines). Saved snapshots themselves are disk-only: "It does not hold memory or running processes" (docs/snapshots).

pause_resume.quote: await sbx.pause() // memory, files and running processes are kept await sbx.resume() // carries on where it left off, usually in about a second
pause_resume.note: The homepage line "Pause & resume: pay nothing while paused" is moot for now: there is no billing yet.

fork.quote: `fork` (or `clone`) copies a running or stopped machine into one new machine, or up to 5 with `--count`.
fork.note: POST /v1/machines/{id}/fork; also new machines from a saved snapshot. Not from a paused machine.

fork_running.quote: `fork` (or `clone`) copies a running or stopped machine into one new machine, or up to 5 with `--count`.
fork_running.note: Disk only: "Memory and running programs are not copied, and the source machine is not changed." A paused machine must be resumed first (409 fork_unavailable).

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Memory and running programs are not copied, and the source machine is not changed.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Forks and snapshots copy disks only; pause keeps memory on the same machine.

persistent_disk.quote: a 20 GiB persistent ext4 disk at `/data` (`/dev/vdb`; home is `/data/home`)
persistent_disk.note: 20 GiB fixed on Free; up to 200 GiB / 500 GiB / 1 TiB on Pro / Builder / Team.

persist_scope.quote: A machine is a Linux VM of your own: its files under /data and the software you install stay across stops and restarts.
persist_scope.note: Both system files (root disk) and /data persist: "Both are kept across stop, pause and start" (OpenAPI).

volumes.quote: Disk (`/data`) | 20 GiB per machine. Free: fixed. A paid machine's grows up to 200 GiB on Pro, 500 GiB on Builder, 1 TiB on Team
volumes.note: No separate volume that outlives a machine is documented; the earlier roadmap item is no longer on the site. Each machine's /data disk persists and grows on paid plans.

volume_attach.quote: Disk (`/data`) | 20 GiB per machine. Free: fixed. A paid machine's grows up to 200 GiB on Pro, 500 GiB on Builder, 1 TiB on Team
volume_attach.note: No separate volume that outlives a machine is documented; the earlier roadmap item is no longer on the site. Each machine's /data disk persists and grows on paid plans.

volume_shared.quote: Disk (`/data`) | 20 GiB per machine. Free: fixed. A paid machine's grows up to 200 GiB on Pro, 500 GiB on Builder, 1 TiB on Team
volume_shared.note: No separate volume that outlives a machine is documented; the earlier roadmap item is no longer on the site. Each machine's /data disk persists and grows on paid plans.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Idle pause | Free: 30 minutes, fixed. Paid plans: 5 to 30 minutes, or off
auto_stop_idle.note: The idle pause keeps memory (suspend), not a stop.

wake_on_request.quote: A visit wakes a machine that paused itself after 30 idle minutes.
wake_on_request.note: Only a machine that paused itself on idle; one you paused or stopped stays offline. A request to a private port without its token does not wake it (docs/idle-suspend).

max_session_h.quote: Max run | Free: 480 minutes at a time, fixed. Paid plans: unlimited by default, or your choice
max_session_h.note: Plan-dependent: Free 8 h (plans[Free].max_session_h); paid plans unlimited.

custom_image.quote: Turn a Docker or OCI image into a snapshot, then start machines from it.
custom_image.note: `instabox snapshot import IMAGE --name N` takes a few minutes and works on every plan; machines then start from that snapshot.

image_oci.quote: Turn a Docker or OCI image into a snapshot, then start machines from it.
image_oci.note: An import step, not an image field on create: the import lays the image's files over the machine's own and saves a snapshot.

docker_inside.quote: Docker : Docker and Docker Compose run inside
docker_inside.note: Docs: "with its own kernel, root and Docker" (docs/concepts); universal template is "dev plus Docker, Python (uv), Go and Rust" (docs/api/account).

nested_virt.quote: Android runs as a container on the machine's own Linux kernel. There is no emulator and no nested VM.
nested_virt.note: /dev/kvm is not documented either way. Android apps run natively through the android template (every plan, Free included).

root.quote: Full VM : a real virtual machine with its own kernel and root
root.note: Exec runs as user dev; files API reads "as root".

browser.quote: Machines from the agent-browser template (shown as base ) have a Linux desktop with a browser.

desktop.quote: Machines from the agent-browser template (shown as base ) have a Linux desktop with a browser. You can watch it, let an agent drive it, and give other people a link to it.
desktop.note: VNC-based. Preinstalled on agent-browser, herdr, orca, android and omarchy; installed on request (about half a minute) on universal and t3 (docs/limits).

computer_use.quote: const png = await sbx.desktop.screenshot() // PNG bytes, e.g. for a vision model await sbx.desktop.click(640, 400)
computer_use.note: Screenshot/click/type/press/scroll/drag primitives; you bring the model ("yourModel.nextAction(png)"). No built-in computer-use agent.

desktop_control.quote: Also: move(x, y) , drag([x1, y1], [x2, y2]) , cursorPosition() , status() .
desktop_control.note: Plus shareable view-only or control stream links (60 s to 24 h, revocable).

ssh.quote: The instabox gateway terminates SSH: ssh -p <port> <machine-id>@<host> , with a short-lived user certificate
ssh.note: Also SSH tokens and mosh. No agent forwarding, X11 or remote forwarding.

public_ipv4.quote: It relays mosh's UDP too, so only the gateway has to be reachable.
public_ipv4.note: Access is through Instabox's SSH gateway and shared HTTPS port domain (https://<port>-<id>.instabox.tech); no per-machine public IP is documented.

inbound_https.quote: A machine has up to 16 published ports.
inbound_https.note: Public by default, token-gated with --private. Raw TCP to a public port is also supported (docs/idle-suspend).

ingress_rules.quote: A private port answers only requests that carry its token.
ingress_rules.note: Public is the default; `--private` gives a token-gated URL (401 without it). No IP allowlists.

open_source.quote: A cloud box for your coding agent, the instabox CLI and its agent skills in one command: npx instabox@latest
open_source.note: The npm CLI wrapper and SDK are labelled Apache-2.0, but their GitHub repositories (InsForge/instabox, InsForge/instabox-sdk) are not public and the server is closed. Not counted as open source.

sso.note: Enterprise plan only (custom price). Other plans sign in with GitHub or Google.

lang_python.quote: "description": "dev plus Docker, Python (uv), Go and Rust"

lang_go.quote: "description": "dev plus Docker, Python (uv), Go and Rust"

lang_rust.quote: "description": "dev plus Docker, Python (uv), Go and Rust"

gpu_desktop.quote: `gpu` | string | none: no GPU | a GPU type your org has access to, count 1

credential_injection.quote: A sandbox sees placeholders, and the outbound proxy adds the credentials to HTTPS headers sent to each Secret's allowed hosts.
credential_injection.note: Org Secrets (proxy, key stays outside the machine) and the personal Vault (written into the machine at boot).

secret_proxy.quote: Encrypted credentials that sandboxes see as placeholders; the outbound proxy adds them to HTTPS headers for allowed hosts.
secret_proxy.note: Since 2026-10-24 (changelog). Headers only (port 443), not URLs or bodies; you list the allowed hosts per Secret. The older personal Vault still writes values into the machine.

live_resize.quote: Changes the idle pause or labels, in any state and at once, or resizes a stopped paid machine: its vCPUs and memory, or its disk (`/data`).
live_resize.note: Resize needs a stop (or `--restart`, which stops, resizes and starts). Free machines cannot be resized.

scoped_api_keys.quote: Full access suits the SDK; Restricted picks scopes:

own_agent_api.note: Instabox provides machines and desktop primitives; the agent and model are the customer's.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: instabox snapshot save dev --name dev-base instabox create --name dev2 --snapshot dev-base
snapshot_on_demand.note: Disk only. Live snapshots: saving a running machine keeps it running, but "the snapshot may leave out data programs have not written to disk yet" (docs/snapshots). Free plan keeps 5; paid plans unlimited; snapshots are free (docs/pricing).

snapshot_auto.quote: In the dashboard: Save snapshot in a machine's menu, then New machine from it , now or later on the Snapshots page.
snapshot_auto.note: Snapshots are user-triggered; the idle pause is a suspend of the machine, not an automatic snapshot.

usage_api.quote: Your machine and snapshot counts, the data they store (measured about hourly) and your limits.
usage_api.note: granularity: account and workspace, with cost (`GET /v1/usage` `cost`: runtime, storage and egress in USD; docs/billing).

max_session_unlimited.quote: Max run | Free: 480 minutes at a time, fixed. Paid plans: unlimited by default, or your choice
max_session_unlimited.note: Paid plans only. Free machines pause after 8 h of running, then a cooldown.

lang_node.quote: gh, Node.js 22 with npm, pnpm and Yarn, Bun, uv, Go, Rust, a JDK (OpenJDK 21)

lang_java.quote: the JDK is OpenJDK 21 (Debian 13 has no 17; `JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-21-openjdk-amd64`)

systemd.quote: Every template but `ci` (Ubuntu 24.04) and `omarchy` (Arch Linux) is Debian 13 (trixie), amd64, with systemd

agent_harnesses.quote: Docker with Compose, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and the desktop (VNC, Xfce, Chromium)
agent_harnesses.note: Preinstalled on agent-browser, herdr and orca; you run the agent yourself. Since 2026-11-01 every box also ships the instabox CLI, agent skills and MCP (changelog).

webhooks.quote: InstaBox now sends a signed POST to your HTTPS endpoint when a sandbox is created, starts, stops
webhooks.note: 2026-10-27. Also pause, failure, deletion and snapshot events; Standard Webhooks format.

mcp_server.quote: Sandbox tools for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode and Antigravity over the Model Context Protocol
mcp_server.note: Hosted at https://api.instabox.sh/mcp; tools create, exec, read and write files, pause and resume sandboxes.

spend_limits.quote: The paid workspace's usage this month reached its spend cap (or its allowance while a payment is past due); its machines cannot run.
spend_limits.note: Set with `instabox workspace spend-cap <workspace> <usd>|off` or in the dashboard.

audit_logs.note: Listed on the Enterprise plan only.

byoc.note: Enterprise plan only; no public detail.

raw_tcp_inbound.quote: A raw TCP connection to a public port | Yes | The connection waits up to 45 seconds for the resume.
raw_tcp_inbound.note: Through the port gateway (TLS), not a per-machine IP.

claims.quote: Machine size | 4 vCPU / 8 GiB by default, the only size on the free plan. Pro: 2/4, 4/8, 8/16. Builder: 2/4 up to 16/32. Team: 2/4 up to 32/64 (vCPUs/GiB).
claims.note: Now the default and Free size; paid plans go to 32/64.

claims.quote: Run the command below. You're in a new machine's shell in under a second.
claims.note: claimed in launch post and on the homepage, not defined in docs; docs only say resume is "usually in about a second" and preboot templates "start faster". Not measured.

claims.quote: Watch a machine's desktop, let an agent drive it, and share a link to it.
claims.note: agent-browser template only; screenshot/click primitives, the model is yours.

claims.quote: Save a machine once, start new ones from it.
claims.note: Disk-only. Live snapshots and fork of a running machine (up to 5 copies) are supported.

claims.quote: Files under /data (home is /data/home ) and the software you install stay.
claims.note: 20 GiB /data per machine, up to 1 TiB on Team.

claims.quote: Give a web server in a machine an HTTPS URL.
claims.note: 16 per machine; public by default, token-gated with --private; wakes an idle-paused machine.
True at the 2026-10-14 launch. Since 2026-10-20 the site shows self-service plans; the API keeps an invite-gate switch.

claims.claim: Early access includes 20 vCPU, 40GB RAM for free
claims.quote: Accounts registered before 2026-10-20 and activated before 2026-10-25 07:45 UTC got five free sandboxes until 2026-12-01 00:00 UTC.
claims.note: 5 x 4/8. Ends 2026-12-01; then one free sandbox runs at a time.

locations_quote: A machine has no `region` field in the API, and create does not take one: a `region` in the body is refused as `400 unknown_field` (create rejects fields it does not know). Placement is the platform's.
